author: Carlos Martinez
title: MOZA SR-P vs Fanatec CSL Pedals LC: Budget Load-Cell Pedals Compared
description: Both bring load-cell braking under ~$200. Here's how the MOZA SR-P and Fanatec CSL Pedals LC actually compare for consistent, repeatable braking in iRacing.

sections.p: If there's one upgrade I'd tell a new iRacing driver to make before anything else on their wheel, it's moving from a spring-based brake pedal to a load cell. I run MOZA CRP2 pedals on my own rig, which sit above this budget tier, but the two pedal sets I get asked about most for readers on a tighter budget are the MOZA SR-P and the Fanatec CSL Pedals LC — both bring genuine load-cell braking in under ~$200.

sections.h2: What a Load Cell Actually Changes

sections.p: A spring-based brake pedal measures travel — how far you push. A load cell measures pressure — how hard you push, regardless of how far the pedal physically moves. That matters because real braking is a pressure input, not a travel input. Once you drive on a load cell, going back to a spring pedal feels vague, like you've lost the ability to feel exactly where lockup starts.

The SR-P is MOZA's budget pedal set, built around a hydraulic-feel brake with a load cell sensor. It's a two or three-pedal set depending on configuration, with adjustable brake resistance via an internal elastomer or spring stack (specifics vary by revision, so check the current spec before buying). In my experience with MOZA's ecosystem generally, build quality at this tier is solid — not flashy, but functional and consistent.

sections.h2: Fanatec CSL Pedals LC: What You Get

sections.p: The CSL Pedals LC adds a load-cell brake module on top of Fanatec's CSL Pedals base, which itself is a widely-used entry pedal set. Fanatec's load-cell module is a well-regarded upgrade path precisely because it's modular — you can start with the base CSL Pedals and add the LC brake kit later rather than buying the whole set at once, which is useful if you're budgeting in stages.

list: MOZA SR-P: integrated load-cell brake, MOZA ecosystem (Pit House software), simpler all-in-one purchase
Fanatec CSL Pedals LC: modular — base pedals + LC brake kit, longer track record, broad third-party damper mod community
Both: adjustable brake resistance, USB connection, suitable for iRacing's brake curve customization

sections.tip: Whichever you buy, spend ten minutes in iRacing's brake calibration screen setting your actual usable pressure range before your first session. A load cell's value disappears if the in-sim curve isn't matched to how hard you can actually press.

sections.p: Fanatec's CSL Pedals have been out longer and have a larger third-party mod community — stiffer elastomers, different brake mod kits, and more documented tuning advice from other sim racers who've been running the same pedal for years. If you like tinkering with brake feel over time, that longer history is worth something. MOZA's ecosystem is newer but growing quickly, and Pit House software covers the core adjustments most people need without requiring hardware mods.

sections.h2: Which One I'd Point You Toward

sections.p: If you want to buy once and be done, the MOZA SR-P is the simpler purchase — one box, load cell included, reasonable price. If you like the idea of starting cheaper and upgrading the brake module later, or you want access to a bigger mod community for fine-tuning brake feel, the Fanatec CSL Pedals LC's modular approach is the better long-term path.

Either way, this is the upgrade that pays off fastest. I'd prioritize a load-cell pedal over a wheel upgrade if you're choosing between the two — braking consistency affects every single corner of every single lap, while wheel FFB detail mostly matters in specific moments.

faqs.q: Is a load-cell pedal really worth it over a spring-based pedal?
faqs.a: Yes, in my experience it's the single highest-impact budget upgrade for consistent braking. A load cell measures pressure rather than travel, which matches how braking actually works and makes threshold braking far easier to repeat lap after lap.

faqs.q: Can I upgrade just the brake pedal and keep my existing throttle and clutch?
faqs.a: With the Fanatec CSL Pedals LC approach, yes — that's the point of the modular design, you can add the load-cell brake module to an existing CSL Pedals base. The MOZA SR-P is typically sold as a complete set rather than piecemeal.

faqs.q: Do I need to adjust in-sim settings after installing a load-cell pedal?
faqs.a: Yes, always calibrate your brake curve in iRacing's control settings after installing a load cell. The default curve won't match your pedal's actual pressure range, and skipping this step is the most common reason people say a new load cell "doesn't feel different."

faqs.q: Will these budget load-cell pedals hold up for serious league racing?
faqs.a: Yes, for the vast majority of sim racers these are genuinely capable of league and official iRacing racing — load-cell braking at this price point is a real upgrade, not a marketing gimmick. The difference versus premium pedals shows up mostly in long-term durability and finer adjustment range, not basic braking consistency.
